articleTitle: Power Definitions for Nonsinusoidal Unbalanced Three-Phase Four-Wire Systems with Different Neutral Conductor Resistance
abstract: This paper defines active currents that minimize line losses while ensuring the same active power transfer to the load in a three-phase four-wire system, where the neutral conductor resistance differs from that of the phase conductors. The problem is analyzed using the calculus of variation technique. The proposed minimization approach results in power definitions that, in specific cases, align with well-established power definitions for sinusoidal, nonsinusoidal, balanced, and unbalanced conditions.

articleTitle: Assessment of the mineral potential of rocks using intelligent data analysis technologies
abstract: This paper presents a study aimed at developing and evaluating a classification model for the mineral potential of geological layers using machine learning methods. The main goal was to create an algorithm capable of predicting the categories of mineral potential — low, medium and high — based on key geological characteristics such as ore content, density, depth, permeability and rock type. The results obtained demonstrated the overall accuracy of the model at 98%, with an almost ideal classification for the categories of medium and high mineral potential. The analysis of the significance of the features showed that the ore content and density have the greatest impact on the classification. The work also revealed certain difficulties in classifying low mineral potential, which is due to limited data or the intersection of characteristics between classes. These results highlight the importance of further research in feature selection and improving data balance. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of using machine learning methods in geological research and their potential for automating mineral resource assessment processes. The developed methodology can be adapted to solve other problems in the field of geology, such as forecasting deposits and optimizing mining.

articleTitle: SCADA Fluid Control System
abstract: This study presents the process of design, development and analysis of a SCADA system for fluid control, in a pumping station, implemented using modern programming environments and simulation platforms. The developed system integrates manual and automatic control functionalities, monitoring via level sensors, as well as automatic switching between main and backup pump in case of technical faults. Integration with SQL Server provides efficient storage and processing of operational data. The web-based application provides visualization of results for tracking and analysis of workflows. The development is applied in the training of students from the bachelor and master courses of electronics, providing them with the opportunity for in-depth learning of the theoretical basics and acquiring practical skills in modern SCADA technologies.

articleTitle: Development of a neural network model for forecasting energy consumption in energy management systems
abstract: This paper explores the use of neural networks to predict energy consumption based on data on the production and use of various fuels, including oil, gas and coal. The aim of the study is to develop a model that can take into account the complex relationships between key parameters such as production volumes, production costs, CO₂ emissions, energy efficiency, inventory levels and transportation costs. The relevance of the study is due to the need to improve the accuracy of forecasting for effective planning and management of resources in the energy industry, especially in conditions of unstable market and environmental factors. In the course of the work, a multi-layered fully connected neural network model was developed, which was trained and tested on the prepared data. The evaluation of the model using the coefficient of determination and the average absolute error demonstrated its high accuracy and suitability for practical application. Additionally, an analysis of the importance of the signs was carried out, which showed that the most significant factors are the import/export of energy and the share of alternative sources. Visualization of the results confirmed that the model is able to make accurate predictions, minimizing errors. The results obtained confirm that the use of neural network models to predict energy consumption is a promising area that can significantly improve decision-making processes in the energy sector and increase resource efficiency.

articleTitle: A Generalized Review of Recent Robotics Research (2020-2024)
abstract: An overview of the current state of robotics is made. A research methodology is created and followed. Results are analyzed and suggestions for further advancements are considered. Future topics and current research on the application of large language models and machine learning in robotics is discussed.

articleTitle: Optimizing static site CMS hosting with Github Codespaces: A cost-effective approach
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of GitHub Codespaces as a strategic tool for optimizing hosting expenses in the realm of Static Site Generation (SSG). With the growing popularity of static sites due to their performance benefits and lower hosting costs, the integration of GitHub Codespaces offers a unique solution for developers seeking to streamline their workflows. We analyze the cost-effectiveness of using Codespaces for development, testing, and deployment processes, highlighting its ability to reduce overhead associated with traditional hosting solutions. Through case studies and comparative analysis, we demonstrate how leveraging Codespaces can lead to significant savings while maintaining high-quality site performance. The obtained results show that GitHub Codespaces enhances productivity and presents a viable financial alternative for developers and organizations focused on efficient static site management.

articleTitle: Study of Power Supply Influence in a Function Generator and Sinusoidal Signal Optimization
abstract: The paper presents a developed functional generator and a study of the influence of the supply voltage on the stability of the frequencies generated by it. Based on experimental studies, the systematic and random errors are calculated and the basic error of each frequency range is determined. Two schematic solutions for the conversion of a triangular to a sinusoidal signal are also proposed, and based on a simulation study in the Matlab programming environment, it is clear that the linear point approximation is the better approach for the conversion of a triangular signal into a sinusoidal one, which is also proved by practical implementation.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of AC-DC Converters in Extreme Fast Charging (XFC) Stations on Grid Quality
abstract: With the increasing demand for electric vehicles (EVs), improving EV specifications is essential. Extreme Fast Charging (XFC) systems can improve the EV user experience by reducing the time spent charging a car's battery. These systems require chargers with high-power capacity. This work presents an assessment of the impact of XFC on the utility grid. Two AC-DC converters that interface XFC with the grid are studied by simulating the charger setups in PSIM®. Vienna three-phase rectifier and three-phase PWM converters were selected for their ability to regulate output voltage and power factor correction functionality. The impact of the two AC-DC converters on the THD and power factor is thoroughly investigated. Although the performance of the two converters is comparative, the result revealed that Vienna offers a wider power operation range without violating the THD limit compared to a three-phase PWM rectifier. The registered THD in the case of the Vienna rectifier is below the 5% threshold if the charger output is above 50% of its rated power. The results suggest that the Vienna rectifier will outperform other topologies in this application.

articleTitle: Derating of dry power transformers in accordance with IEEE Std. C57.110 and EN 50541-2
abstract: Current and voltage harmonics generated by nonlinear elements in electric power systems cause increased heating of power transformers due to additional core losses, eddy current losses, skin effect, etc. Consequently, in some cases, derating the power transformer's maximum operating capacity must be done. This paper analyzes the necessity of derating dry power transformers following IEEE Std. C57.110 and EN 50541-2. Calculations are done for results measured at two locations: 1) PV power plant (voltage level 0.8 kV, the maximum measured power 1460 kVA), and 2) small hydropower plant supplying large nonlinear loads (voltage level 10 kV, the maximum measured power 840 kVA). More critical results are estimated using IEEE Std. C57.110 and in the case of the small hydropower plant supplying large nonlinear loads.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Systems with Fractional Dynamics and Algebraic Constraints
abstract: This study investigates optimal control problems described by fractional differential equations, with the control vector components subject to algebraic constraints. Two case studies are analyzed: an illustrative example designed to test the algorithm’s effectiveness and a biologically significant model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), which applies optimal control theory to design therapeutic strategies under medical constraints. The methodology transforms fractional differential equations into equivalent ordinary differential equations using the framework of Atanacković and Stanković. L.S. Pontryagin’s maximum principle is then applied to derive control functions that satisfy the algebraic constraints, followed by numerical optimization of the Hamiltonian function. We formally parsed the problem of dynamic optimization into a static optimization problem using the Forward-Backward Sweep Method (FBSM). The approach is validated through comprehensive numerical simulations, demonstrating its robustness and applicability to real-world problems.

articleTitle: Leveraging STEM Approaches in Extracurricular Robotics Activities to Enhance Digital Competencies in Informatics Education
abstract: This paper explores the impact of integrating extracurricular STEM robotics activities as a method for enhancing digital skills in informatics education. The research focuses on an author' training model implemented in a school robotics club, designed to support and develop competencies in informatics through STEM methodology. The pedagogical experiment involves diagnostic assessments and project-based evaluations. The findings suggest that STEM robotics activities effectively foster key digital competencies and increase student engagement in informatics. This study contributes to the STEM’s role in education and offers a model for skill-building through applied technology in extracurricular settings.

articleTitle: STEM Educational Game "Young Engineer" to Improve the Digital Competence of Students
abstract: In a time when digital competencies become even more important, among the students prepared to be future computer systems and technology engineers, a steady trend of decreasing interest in computer hardware has been observed. It looks like the predictions from the early 21st century that the children of the digital generation would be more likely to use digital technologies than to create them have turned out to be true. But the training of engineers in this field requires knowledge of at least the principles of Boolean logic, the basic logic gates, and the basic sequential and combinational circuits - the so-called "glue" logic because the lack of elementary knowledge in this area makes it difficult to study and design more complex digital systems. Interest in this subject should be encouraged at school age by appropriately introducing the "glue" logic to the students. STEM education is beginning to be massively applied in the school educational system but studying basic logic circuits and devices is weakly, let's say not at all, being presented within the abundance and variety of STEM lessons. The development of a STEM educational game for learning the principle of operation of basic logic gates and how they work together, connected in a circuit diagram, will contribute to increasing the interest in digital logic devices, and hence to easier teaching at university courses related to the design of various digital systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Resistor Selection and Matching for Desired Resistance
abstract: In precision control engineering, selecting the appropriate servo drive is crucial for tasks such as micrometer or nanometer positioning and maintaining speed stability at extremely low velocities. Traditional pulse-width modulation servo drives introduce current ripple, which in turn causes force ripple, limiting precision. To address this, non-switching linear amplifiers offer a viable alternative, providing high-quality output and improved dynamic performance, despite their lower efficiency. A key challenge in designing high-output current, low-supply voltage, linear amplifiers is ensuring uniform current distribution among parallel-connected bipolar junction transistors. Unequal current sharing leads to thermal stress, significantly reducing reliability and component lifespan. This paper explores the impact of emitter resistor tolerance on transistor current balancing and proposes a systematic method for resistor selection and pairing. This approach is particularly valuable in scenarios where precise low-tolerance resistors are not readily available, and large-scale serial production is not feasible.

articleTitle: A method for geolocating distant objects using a MEMS gyroscope
abstract: This paper presents a new method for geolocating distant objects using a MEMS (micro-electromechanical systems) gyroscope and available GPS (Geographics Positioning System) coordinates of the measurement positions. Using this method, GPS coordinates of a distant object can be calculated based on two successive gyroscope measurements of the angle which forms the distant object and horizontal line. The measurements can be taken from an UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) or manually from the ground, where GPS signal is available. Accuracy of the method has been tested experimentally using the developed embedded system based on the STM32F103 microcontroller, gyroscope MPU-6050 and NEO-6M GPS module.

articleTitle: Application of Intelligent Modeling Techniques for Optimizing Coal Mining Operations
abstract: The article is devoted to application of intellectual modeling methods for optimization of coal mining processes. Various approaches to increase productivity and reduce costs through optimal resource planning and prediction of technical failures are considered. Different scenarios of machinery operation, including changes in the number of equipment and shift duration, were analyzed in the study. Predictive models showed that the use of intelligent approaches can significantly reduce fuel costs, decrease equipment downtime and improve the overall efficiency of coal mining operations. Experimental results confirm that the proposed solutions contribute to achieving optimal production performance and more rational use of resources.

articleTitle: Interaction through bionic signals. Overview
abstract: The paper examines the possibilities of bionic technology as a means of communication with a computer system. A classification of the most commonly used signal detection technologies is carried out. A model of a system using this technology is presented. An overview of the possibilities of the application of such systems in the daily life of the mass consumer has been carried out.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Leading Backend Frameworks for Developers
abstract: Software developers often need guides navigating them in the process of choosing the most suitable frameworks and programming languages for their needs. In this study, the impact of the programming languages on the performance of four popular backend frameworks: Spring Boot, ASP.NET Core, Express.js, and Django is examined using tools such as Apache JMeter and Docker under uniform conditions. With metrics like latency, throughput, docker build time, and deployment time the experiments revealed that ASP.NET Core exhibited the lowest latency (1ms for HTTP POST and GET), while Django achieved the shortest deployment time (0.31 seconds). Spring Boot and Express.js occupied the middle ground, balancing flexibility and performance. Besides valuable insights into the efficiency of each framework in real-world applications, this paper also includes a review of similar studies while complementing them by providing additional perspectives through concrete measurements and analyses under realistic conditions. This study contributes to a better understanding of architectural decisions and their relationship to performance while making the way for further research, such as analyzing more complex applications and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Algorithm and Implementation of Simulation Study of Linear (6, 3) Block Codes Using Spreadsheets
abstract: The importance of linear block codes for modern communication systems justifies the need for the research presented in the publication. The paper describes an algorithm and developed MS Excel-based module for simulation research of linear (6, 3) block codes, which will be used in the training process in the course "Coding in Telecommunication Systems", included as an elective in the curriculum of the specialty "Internet and Mobile Communications", for the educational and qualification degree "Bachelor", at the University of Ruse. The module allows the investigation of 24 options of linear (6, 3) block codes based on the generator and control matrices. The laws for coding and verification of the considered linear block codes are derived. The module allows tracing the process of obtaining the codeword for a given information sequence (Encoder), as well as the process of detecting and correcting a single error for a given codeword (Decoder). The developed training module contributes to the educational process by increasing students' understanding of encoding and decoding concepts, increasing the interest of students studying the course "Coding in Telecommunication Systems" and improving their practical skills. It also serves to automate the procedure of generating assignments for independent work of students during practical exercises. Using MS Excel, the module provides an interactive platform that facilitates students' learning and makes complex concepts more accessible. Future work envisages the expansion of the module with the inclusion of other linear block (n, k)-codes. Expanding the module with new linear block codes will improve the learning experience and highlight the importance of adapting educational resources to new technologies.

articleTitle: Ship Detection Software Based on High-Resolution Algorithms for Primary Signal Processing: From Idea to Implementation in HFSWRs
abstract: In recent years, maritime surveillance of ships using High Frequency Surface Wave Radars (HFSWRs) represents very important challenge, where most attention is focused on algorithms for primary signal processing and the implementation of such algorithms to make them applicable in real-time. This paper contains an overview of the high-resolution primary signal processing in HFSWRs, as well as its implementation using C programming language. All the necessary input data and parameters of the algorithms are described, then the way of executing the program, and finally the output data. A real-time operation is achieved thanks to the implementation based on multithreading by improving the existing implementation of the high-resolution range-Doppler map estimation, which is the most computationally demanding task. As a part of software infrastructure, we have developed a set of auxiliary processing components, allowing end-users graphical presentation of processed radar data. We have demonstrated the capabilities of the ship detection software which can be execute on general purpose computers, and where processing can be performed in real-time or subsequently, for the needs of which an additional program has been developed, thus forming a ship detection software package.

articleTitle: Implementation of RFID System for Industrial Applications
abstract: The industrial sector increasingly relies on innovative technologies to optimize workflows and improve traceability. The paper presents the development of an Ultra-High Frequency (UHF) RFID-based system designed for seamless tracking and management of physical objects in industrial environments. The proposed device reads RFID tags, collects supplementary data, and transmits it to a central server for integration into the company’s digital systems. The system was implemented in a grain processing company, where it demonstrated high reliability, adaptability, and operational benefits. By automating tasks like inventory tracking and production monitoring, the RFID system streamlined processes, minimized errors, and provided real-time insights. Additionally, the flexibility of the device’s configuration and its integration with existing systems underscore its scalability for various industrial applications.

articleTitle: Filtering MEMS Gyroscope Data: A Comparative Analysis of Noise Reduction Methods : Student paper
abstract: This study compares three filtering techniques for removing noise in the MEMS MPU-6050 gyroscope, including Kalman, Bessel, and Exponential Moving Average filters. Parameter selection was conducted through experimental, iterative testing for every algorithm. The UAV (drone) experiment with a mounted MPU-6050 gyroscope obtained 171 raw, noisy tilt angle measurements around the x-axis. The UAV hovered above the ground while taking angle measurements, and the effects of high vibrations from the drone’s motor to MPU-6050 were observed with filter solutions. Analysis techniques like variance and cross-correlation with quadratic interpolation showed the preferable filtering solution in dynamic scenarios where latency and smoothness are critical.

articleTitle: Implementation of automated information system at a textile enterprise
abstract: This article examines the implementation of an automated information system in a textile company in order to increase the efficiency and productivity of the enterprise. The main subject of the study is the process of implementing the system, including the selection of a pilot project, testing and optimization, as well as gradual implementation to other areas of production. The important stages of the study were setting up a pilot system, testing and optimization, as well as gradual implementation of the system in different areas of production. The results of the study showed that the introduction of an automated information system made it possible to improve control over production operations, reduce resource costs and time, and improve the quality of products. The findings of this study highlight the importance of introducing automated information systems in the textile industry to ensure the competitiveness of enterprises. The presented results may be useful for companies seeking to optimize their production processes and improve their position in the textile market.

articleTitle: Estimation of Emotion from Speech through Analysis of Fundamental Frequency Derivative
abstract: In this paper, we conducted an analysis of speaker emotions through speech evaluation. The Introduction section introduces an algorithm designed to assess emotional speech, which is grounded in the examination of the fundamental frequency path (F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>). This assessment employs a decision line derived from the first derivative of the frequency, utilizing a positive and negative frequency increment. The CTD algorithm that establishes criteria for detecting emotions in plane $\left( {\begin{array}{ll} {{F_0},}&{F_{0, + - }^{(1)}} \end{array}} \right)$ is described. The decision criterion distinguishing between Normal and Boredom emotions was defined during the preliminary training phase based on the testing emotions from Base. The next section of the paper presents an experiment focusing on the statistical evaluation of accuracy concerning speaker emotion classification. To evaluation the efficacy of emotional estimations, a confusion matrix was utilized. The results from these experiments are presented both in tabular and graphical formats.

articleTitle: Analysis of derating necessity of oil-immersed 10/0.4 kV/kV power transformers–the case studies of four PV power plants
abstract: In the last few years many PV power plants have been connected to the electric distribution network. They are nonlinear sources of electric power and consequently generate current harmonics. These harmonics cause heating of power transformers due to the additional eddy current and core losses, skin effect, etc. This paper analyzes the necessity of derating power transformers installed at the points of common coupling (PCC) of PV power plants. Calculations are done in accordance with EN 50464-3:2007. Four two-winding three-phase oil-immersed 10/0.4 kV/kV power transformers with rated power equal to 150 kVA (two of them), 250 kVA, and 1250 kVA are analyzed. In all cases, it is presented that there is no need to derating power transformers because analyzed PV inverters generate low current harmonics at medium and high power.

articleTitle: Employing Pretrained Networks for Reducing the Latency and the Complexity of a Radio Frequency Fingerprinting System
abstract: This study proposes an approach employing a number of trained networks for radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting to reduce the latency and the complexity of the identification system. The networks are trained using identification signals with different durations which are determined based on their SNR levels. RF fingerprints are obtained from these signals by extracting features. In the testing stage of RF fingerprinting, for each test signal, one of the pretrained networks is selected according to the estimated SNR value of the received signal and classification is carried out by this network. We utilize an experimental dataset comprising IEEE 802.11n signals captured from 20 Wi-Fi transmitters to evaluate the performance of the proposed approach. The experimental results demonstrate that, instead of relying on a long fixed-duration, we can utilize pretrained networks to achieve lower latency and reduced computational complexity while maintaining high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Novel Call Records Archiving Approach for High-speed Railway Lines in Serbia
abstract: Call recording and archiving are essential components of the railway safety system, ensuring communication transparency and enabling the reconstruction of events and incidents. These systems capture and store conversations for analysis, safety compliance, training and incident investigation. Traditionally, call recording and archiving were managed by the, so-called, registrophone, a hardware device designed to capture voice communication among railway personnel. However, with the infrastructure softwarization, the functionalities of the registrophone have been distributed across several components. This paper discusses the Central Call Records Archive CRS (srb. Centralni Registar Snimaka) archiving solution which addresses the challenges posed by the softwarization of the registrophone. The new fault-tolerant solution ensures the reliability, scalability, and seamless integration with the existing infrastructure, focusing on secure and reliable data storage, resilient processes and cryptographic methods to provide data integrity, prevent data loss in unforeseen circumstances and guarantee call record origin. The proposed system enhances the railway telecommunications infrastructure, providing a more efficient and robust solution for managing call recordings and archives. The presented call record archiving was designed for Railway Dispatcher Central System SPDC (srb. Sistem Pružne Dispečerske Centrale) realized in high-speed railway lines in the Republic of Serbia.

articleTitle: Balancing Neural Network Training Convergence with Efficient Computational Boundaries
abstract: The neural network training process produces black-box models with low explainability. In addition, the process itself is numerical, with parameters (such as learning rate, momentum, and early stopping trigger) being chosen ad hoc. During the training with chosen parameters, after each calculated update of the weights, the observed total change of weights indicates which training stage the network is currently in. At the same time, neural networks are limited in the data they can model due to various reasons, such as architecture, activation functions, data itself, and the training approach. This limitation is expressed in the phenomenon of the efficient computational frontier, which, it seems, cannot be crossed, no matter the hyperparameters of the network. This paper tackles the efficient usage of information regarding the total change of weights and the efficient computational frontier to determine when the training should be stopped. The results demonstrate the efficiency of training of simpler models compared to more complex models and prove that the general weight structure of models is formed very quickly in the training, while the forming of finer details takes up much more time.

articleTitle: A Stochastic Modeling and Artificial Neural Network-Based Method for Electric and Magnetic Field Reduction Near Overhead Transmission Lines
abstract: This paper considers the approach for overhead transmission lines’ (OHTL) electric and magnetic field reduction by finding the best phase conductors (PCs) and shield wires (SWs) positions. This approach combines an algorithm based on stochastic modeling for OHTL configuration generation, with the artificial neural networks (ANN) based method for the electric field strength and magnetic flux density determination. This approach enables the generation of an arbitrary number of different OHTL configurations, taking into account specific user-defined limitations. This further, enables to find the OHTL designs that are the best solution for the considered case study regarding electric and magnetic field levels. In this paper, a case study is presented where the considered approach is employed to find the OHTL designs that give the best results regarding the limitation of electric and magnetic field values.

articleTitle: Security Aspects of Container Orchestration in Kubernetes Environments
abstract: Security is one of the key challenges in container orchestration, especially in complex environments. This paper explores the security aspects of implementing containerized applications using Docker within a Kubernetes cluster. The first part of the paper describes Docker, Kubernetes, and various ways of applying them within DevOps methodology. It then presents potential vulnerabilities during the implementation of these technologies, as well as vulnerabilities specific to Docker and Kubernetes. Subsequently, some solutions for securing a Kubernetes environment are described.

articleTitle: Effect of Cellulose Contaminant on Dielectric Strength of Circulated Synthetic Ester Oil
abstract: This study focuses on the investigation on the effects of circulation velocity and various cellulose contaminants to the dielectric strength of circulated synthetic ester oil under AC Voltage. A specialized chamber was devised to replicate the circulation conditions of oil within an operational transformer. The experimental findings indicate that higher concentrations of cellulose contaminant correlated with a reduction in AC breakdown voltage (AC-BDV). Conversely, an increase in circulation velocity leads to an enhancement in the AC-BDV of the samples, whether they are pure or contaminated with cellulose. To validate these findings, simulations utilizing the Finite Element Method (FEM) were conducted. The examination of the electric field distribution indicated that the presence of cellulose impurities intensified the electric field strength, whereas the circulation acted to mitigate this phenomenon.

articleTitle: Effects of Core Pin Hole Size and Placement on No-Load Losses in Power Transformers
abstract: This study examines the influence of core pinhole size and location on the performance of a 5 MVA transformer, focusing on core losses such as eddy current and hysteresis losses. Simulations were conducted using Finite Element Method (FEM) across scenarios with varying pinhole diameters (10, 15, and 20 mm) and positions (P0, P1, P2). Results indicate that smaller pinholes positioned near P0 which is closer to the corner of the core minimize core losses, while larger diameters and central placements increase losses due to magnetic flux disruption. These findings provide a basis for optimizing transformer core designs to enhance efficiency and balance structural requirements.

articleTitle: A Study on Global Cyclicality of the S&P 500 Index Using a Hybrid Model of Recurrent Neural Networks and Fourier Transformations
abstract: The S&P 500 index is one of the most important and widely followed indices in capital markets. It serves as an indicator of the state of the U.S. economy, making it a compelling subject of study. This article presents a study on the existence of global cyclicality in the dynamics of the S&P 500 index. For this purpose, a hybrid analytical approach has been applied, combining Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks with spectral analysis using Fourier transformations. The conducted experiments identified a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) that accurately approximates the index’s movement over the period from 2014 to 2024. However, no global cyclicality was found in the S&P 500 data, indicating that the index’s movements are predominantly chaotic and nonlinear, without stable and recurring global patterns. Short-term cyclicality with a period of 80–90 days was identified.

articleTitle: Analysis of Torque Ripple Reduction in Synchronous Reluctance Machines when Applying Different Control Strategies
abstract: This paper discusses and analyzes static control strategies to reduce torque ripple in Synchronous Reluctance Machines (SynRMs). The analyzed control strategies leveraged trading an acceptable conduction power loss increase concerning Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) operation to reduce torque ripple. The results showed the feasibility of peak-to-peak torque ripple reduction, which could support the reduction of the fundamental component of the torque ripple with active control approaches.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Analysis of Active Filters with a Single-Loop Negative Feedback
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology for synthesizing and analyzing low-pass, high-pass, and band-pass active filters with an operational amplifier and a single-loop negative feedback. Simulation results of the synthesized filters in MicroCAP are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of the peak load of 10 kV line "Vučko" from the 35/10 kV transformer station Jahorina
abstract: The paper shows the calculation of the peak power of a certain consumption area, the simultaneous peak load during the period of the highest consumption of electricity on the 10 kV line "Vučko". A large number of the most diverse consumers participate in the formation of the peak load of consumption, that is, the peak load of the elements of the electrical distribution system. The load on consumers is generally variable over time. A detailed analysis of these data provides the continuity (reliability) of the power supply. The obtained calculation results in the amount of 3.62 MVA represent the highest peak load of the given transformer area. By comparing the calculation results with the remote reading of the peak load that the electricity supplier has, an accuracy of 95% is obtained. The calculation example itself represents a reliable way to determine the peak load where there is no remote reading.

articleTitle: An Experimentally-Based Method For Detection Threshold Determination in HFSWR’s High-Resolution Range-Doppler Map Target Detection
abstract: Primary signal processing in High Frequency Surface Wave Radars (HFSWRs) plays an important role because it affects their overall performance. The two most important parameters in high-resolution primary signal processing, which is based on the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm, are the boundary between the signal subspace and the noise subspace in the eigenvalue decomposition process, and detection threshold used for target detection on range-Doppler (RD) map. With most of the existing radars, detection is generally performed in the RD domain, and then the azimuth is estimated only for the detected targets. Therefore, target detectability is primarily determined by target detectability performance in the RD domain. This paper shows that the determination of the detection threshold based on experimental results is possible by forming Radar Operating Characteristics (ROC) for individual ships, in order to see how the radar actually works in practice, but also to estimate the optimal value of the detection threshold, so that the probability of target detection is satisfactory.

articleTitle: Needle Grippers For Non-Rigid Materials
abstract: Automated handling of non-rigid and of non-metallic deformable materials poses unique challenges due to their deformable nature and different characteristics under different conditions. Traditional grippers used in mechanical and electrical engineering are not suitable for these tasks. The increasing use of synthetic materials requires specialized grippers, especially when working with fabrics, leather, textiles and some foodstuffs that can deform under their weight.Grippers are classified into mechanical, vacuum, magnetic and other types. For non-solid materials, three main classes are identified: mechanical, needle and planar grippers. Needle grippers, which pierce materials with needles, are particularly effective for porous objects. The design of needle grippers varies with needle type, piercing method, drive type and material, allowing customization for different materials, applications and conditions.Experimental research conducted at the University of Ruse is aimed at optimizing needle grippers for textiles and synthetic materials. Key parameters such as punching force and inclination angle are critical for effective design and operation. The results show that the optimal punching force varies with needle diameter and inclination, highlighting the need for experimental validation in gripper design. These findings enhance the application of needle grippers in industrial automation, providing efficient handling without damaging materials.

articleTitle: Modifying Blowfish Algorithm Using Permutation Techniques
abstract: This paper proposes a modified version of the Blowfish Algorithm using permutation techniques. These techniques are key parts of the F-function of the algorithm. The first modification is in the bit operations while the second part employs the cyclical Shift Rows operation. We conducted simulations to test the security strength of the modified Blowfish Algorithm in changing one bit from two input strings. The avalanche effect showed 54.687% and 53.125% changes in the output bits thus making our model secure. We also tested the execution performance of the original Blowfish Algorithm and the modified Blowfish Algorithm in the encryption and decryption processes. While the original version performs better than the modified version, no statistical difference was found between the two versions.

articleTitle: Single-source Publishing using Starfish UPTEP Method: Applications in Multilingual Web Site Development and Courseware Content Management
abstract: Single-source publishing has been known for decades as a method of creating and maintaining published content from a single source document, while generating different content forms. It has usually been associated with the maintenance of a system documentation and it has been implemented in specialized systems around certain particular document forms. We present a case that such an approach would be useful in an open-ended general area of text-based document management applications, such as creation and maintenance of multi-lingual web sites and courseware material maintenance in LaTeX. Such application areas are very dynamic and open in types of target text, which is used for further processing and document rendering, so a closed system for single-source publishing would not be appropriate. We demonstrate an approach using universal text preprocessing and text-embedded programming (UPTEP) that can be effectively used for this task. This solution approach is validated through the use of open-source Starfish system, which is a general UPTEP system. We show how the UPTEP approach to single-source publishing can be readily implemented using Starfish on the two case studies.

articleTitle: PROFINET Controller on Cloud
abstract: PROFINET (Process Field Network) is an industrial Ethernet standard widely used for real-time data communication in automation systems, with over 60 million active nodes as of 2024. It facilitates fast and reliable cyclic data transmission, enabling real-time monitoring and control between devices such as programmable logic controllers (PLCs), sensors, and actuators. Traditionally, controllers and devices needed to operate within close physical proximity to ensure successful IO data exchange. However, advancements in network technology now allow PROFINET IO data to be transmitted over VPN connections with acceptable latency. This development enables real-time data to be redirected from factory-level devices to cloud systems, overcoming hardware limitations, enabling data storage and analysis, and supporting complex algorithms for more flexible and efficient production. This study investigates the feasibility and benefits of using a PROFINET controller deployed on a cloud virtual machine and communicating over VPN technology, with a focus on the efficiency and communication characteristics between the controller and its network.

articleTitle: Comparison of IMC and Cross-Coupling Decoupling Current Regulation Structures in PMSM Drives
abstract: In this paper, two types of the current regulation in an electric drive with permanent magnet synchronous motor are analyzed. The first one is based on the principle of cross-coupling decoupling, and the second one is based on the concept of the internal model. The derivation of the equations and the synthesis of the parameters for the current PI controllers in the s-domain and z-domain are presented. The performance of both current regulation topologies were tested through computer simulations in permanent magnet synchronous motor drive.

articleTitle: Evaluating Extended Kalman Filter and Unscented Kalman Filter for accurate trajectory estimation
abstract: This paper evaluates two common methods for trajectory estimation: the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), the Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF). The EKF and UKF are well-established recursive filtering techniques commonly used for nonlinear state estimation.The performance of these methods is compared through their implementation on a standard trajectory estimation problem, with a focus on assessing their accuracy.

articleTitle: Mapping the Research Topics and Patterns related to Assistive Technology: a Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Assistive technology (AT) enhances autonomy and social participation for individuals with disabilities and serves as a valuable educational tool. This study maps AT research topics and trends using bibliometric analysis of articles from the Web of Science database which was performed during 2023. Co-citation and keyword co-occurrence analysis were conducted, and results visualized using VoS Viewer. The study identifies key authors, publishers, countries, and collaboration trends, highlighting AT research’s rapid evolution driven by emerging technologies and user needs. Common keywords reveal major themes, including AT itself, its users, accessibility, and disabilities connected to the use of AT. The study underscores AT’s complexity, interdisciplinarity, and alignment with technological and social needs, emphasizing the importance of collaboration, innovation, and data-driven policies.

articleTitle: Digital ASIC Implementation of a 0.8-GHz Multi-Accelerator Computing Cluster Using Hammer Flow
abstract: Each new silicon process VLSI node brings significant changes to the RTL-to-GDSII Tcl backend flow, often requiring the manual rewriting of ASIC digital Tcl scripts from scratch. In this paper, we review the Hammer RTL-to-GDSII flow, a modular platform designed to reduce redundant efforts in writing new Tcl scripts when designers switch technology nodes or change EDA tool vendors. We highlight the key strengths of this flow and identify areas for improvement.

articleTitle: Developing a 2D game engine to simplify tile-based platformer development : Student paper
abstract: In today’s world, entertainment is playing an ever-growing role in people’s lives. With video games becoming the leading form of entertainment, outgrowing the music and film industries, there is now, more than ever, an interest in making video games and putting your hand into this pot of gold. The essential part of every game is its engine, which is the code in charge of handling complex tasks such as rendering, physics simulation, scene management, etc. This paper presents a simplified way of creating a game for developers new to game development by creating a simple 2D game engine named Blazr, accompanied by an intuitive editor.

articleTitle: Applying Probability Method for Battery Electric Vehicle Selection
abstract: The global automotive industry is actively transitioning to the production of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) to significantly reduce carbon emissions and contribute to a greener planet. The proliferation of BEVs is not only a trend but also an urgent solution to address climate change. In the context of a world striving for sustainable development, choosing the right electric vehicle becomes a crucial decision for consumers. This study, for the first time, applies the probability method to select an electric vehicle from ten available options. Each electric vehicle is described by 11 criteria, and the weights of these criteria have been calculated using three different methods: MEREC, CRITIC, and equal weights. This study found that regardless of the method used to weigh the criteria, the probabilistic method consistently identified the best BEV. Furthermore, the BEV identified as the best using the probabilistic method coincided with those found using the PIV, TOPSIS, and SAW methods. This research has pioneered in demonstrating the accuracy of the probability method when used to rank BEVs.

articleTitle: Computing Descriptive Statistics of Bluetooth Signals Using a Neural Network
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to analyzing Bluetooth signals using deep learning with neural networks. Due to their complex properties, Bluetooth signals require advanced methods for analysis. Thes neural network model predicts the mean and standard deviation of these signals, utilizing fully connected layers and Tanh and Softmax activation functions. Model performance is evaluated with metrics such as MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R-squared. The research demonstrates that neural networks can accurately extract statistical features from Bluetooth signals, contributing to improvements in wireless communication by optimizing signal analysis and error detection.

articleTitle: Intelligent model for assessing the suitability of water based on its chemical and biological parameters
abstract: This paper presents a study on the development and testing of a machine learning model for classifying water according to its purpose, based on chemical and microbiological indicators. The aim of the study is to create an accurate and stable model that can effectively determine the categories of water — drinking, industrial, agricultural and technical — based on the analysis of its qualitative characteristics. The gradient boosting method was chosen as the algorithm for classification, which demonstrated high accuracy and reliability when working with multidimensional data. The study included the processing of a synthetic dataset containing information on water parameters such as calcium concentration, total bacterial content, phosphate levels, alkalinity, sulfates and oxidizability. The analysis of the correlation matrix made it possible to identify the relationships between the features, which made it possible to optimize the operation of the model and improve its accuracy. The quality of the model was tested using accuracy, completeness and F1-score metrics, which demonstrated almost perfect results for all categories. In conclusion, it is concluded that the proposed model can be successfully used to automate the analysis of water quality in ecology, industry and agriculture. The use of intelligent technologies opens up new opportunities for monitoring water resources, increasing the efficiency and reliability of quality control.

articleTitle: Proposal of Fast Locking VHF PLL Synthesizer
abstract: Fast Locking Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) Synthesizers play a key role in many applications that require rapid stabilization of frequency and phase. Fast PLL locking is particularly important in Frequency-Hopping Spread Spectrum (FHSS), frequency-agile radars, quantum computing, multi-core processors, and more. This paper presents a new technique for fast locking of PLL synthesizers, based on applying the appropriate pre-bias voltage to the PLL filter and then resetting Phase Frequency Detector (PFD) and counters to achieve initial phase alignment between the reference signal and the divided VCO signal. This approach significantly reduces the PLL settling time, which is also confirmed by the measurement results provided in this paper.

articleTitle: Flash Memory Based Performance Analysis on PROFINET Devices
abstract: This paper presents a comparative performance analysis of SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) NOR, Quad SPI (QSPI) NOR, and Parallel NOR flash memory technologies in conjunction with the ERTEC 200P-3 microcontroller. The ERTEC 200P-3, an ARM-based controller developed by Siemens, is specifically designed for PROFINET industrial communication applications and is widely utilized in the PROFINET IO device market, encompassing products such as servo drives and I/O modules. The primary objective of this study is to assist manufacturers in selecting the most efficient and cost-effective flash memory solution for their PROFINET IO devices. The analysis evaluates critical performance metrics, including boot-up times, read/write speeds, and communication speeds, which directly influence system performance and responsiveness. Additionally, a cost analysis of the flash memory technologies is conducted to provide a comprehensive evaluation from both performance and economic perspectives.

articleTitle: Empirical Relation of Second Optical Transition Energies of Metallic Single Wall Carbon Nanotubes with their Chirality
abstract: In this work we have examined the empirical relationship between the second optical transition energies (E22) and the chirality of metallic single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs). By deriving a quick and effective method, an empirical formula that predicts optical energy based on chiral indices (n, m) of the SWCNTs. Here, we compiled a range of SWCNTs with chiral indices from (4, 0) to (20, 20) and calculated their diameters and M22 values, which were then compared to empirical data from previous studies. With this suggested approach, the chiral index of metallic SWCNT can be used to directly assume its second optical transition energy. The experimental data is compared with the expected results. The average error between the computed and experimental values was determined, to visually present the findings, named the Katuara plot.

articleTitle: Discrete Cosine Transform-based Data Compression of Bioimpedance with Embedded Hardware
abstract: This study explores the application of the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to compress multi-frequency bioimpedance datasets that are well represented by the Cole-impedance model. The motivating goal is to reduce the data storage and wireless transmission requirements of these datasets to support portable and wearable systems that utilize this type of data. To evaluate the compression, DCT was applied to both synthetic and experimentally obtained datasets using MATLAB and an embedded-hardware environment (Arduino IDE and XIAO BLE board). Using this approach, compression ratios exceeding 98% were obtained for noiseless datasets, and up to 95% for noisy datasets, and 93% for experimental datasets. This validates the feasibility of using this DCT-based compression method for bioimpedance data to advance portable and wearable systems. Future efforts will focus on improving noise resilience and optimizing embedded hardware implementations.

articleTitle: Maximum Torque Per Ampere Control of Brushless DC Motors with Misaligned Hall Sensors
abstract: Three-Phase Hall-Sensor-controlled brushless DC (BLDC) motors are widely used in many industrial and electric mobility applications due to their high efficiency, power density, and cost-effectiveness. A typical voltage-source inverter (VSI) with the 120° commutation controls the motor's stator currents based on the Hall sensor signals that give the rotor position at discrete intervals. However, many low-cost motors often have misaligned Hall sensors, leading to distorted switching sequences and degraded performance. Furthermore, the BLDC motors with large winding inductance have non-negligible commutation intervals that shift the operation angle away from the desirable maximum torque-per-Ampere (MTPA) operation. This paper extends the previous research in this area and combines the filtering of Hall sensor signals with the automatic correction of the commutation angle to maintain the MTPA operation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated on a typical industrial motor with a large electrical time constant and misalignment of Hall sensors.

articleTitle: 2D Analysis of Solid Iron Rotor Induction Machines
abstract: This paper presents a new 2D analytical modeling of solid iron rotor induction motors. Magnetic rotor iron saturation, skin effect, rotor curvature, and third dimension effect are considered in the 2D modeling. The analytical results for the torque at different speeds are compared with the 2D finite element method and experimental results to evaluate the accuracy of analytical modeling.

articleTitle: Assessment of Load and Wind Power Uncertainty Modeling on Power Flow Analysis for Distribution Systems
abstract: Harnessing renewable energy in modern power systems demands precise modeling of uncertainties to ensure efficient and reliable operation and planning. This study investigates the intricate effects of load and wind power uncertainty on power flow results for distribution systems by employing two distinct scenario-based methodologies. The first approach integrates temporal harmony between load and wind power data, clustering them simultaneously to create cohesive scenarios. Conversely, the second approach independently models load and wind power scenarios before combining them to capture variability. In order to obtain clusters, k-means clustering method is utilized in both methods where 10000 scenarios are generated using Normal and Weibull distributions for load and wind power, respectively. These methodologies are applied to a modified 33-bus radial distribution system, examining power flows, voltage profiles, and power losses under different number of scenarios.

articleTitle: Sounding of Websites and Portals in Serbian Language
abstract: The paper presents the principle of voicing Internet sites and portals in the Serbian language, among which is the eUprava portal - a national web portal that represents a unique access point to electronic administration in the Republic of Serbia, where electronic administration services are implemented. The operating procedures of the text and speech processing module are given, as well as the principle of speech synthesis for the Serbian language based on HMM Hidden Markov Models. At the end, the concept of sounding the eUprava portal in Serbian was provided.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of standard image segmentation methods
abstract: Image segmentation is key process in image analysis which is based on separating "objects of interest" from the rest of the image. This represents the first step in obtaining meaningful information from the images, this enabling further analysis of the identified components. In this paper a comparative analysis of standard methods for image segmentation, namely the K-means algorithm, the Watershed algorithm and the Region Growing algorithm, was performed. For this research were used real-life image from BSD500 image database, specifically 200 Training Images – Berkeley Segmentation Dataset. After the segmentation of the image, the results were processed first with the mathematical indicators PSNR and then with the metric for assessing the accuracy of the model with F1 Score metrics. The obtained results show that for the PSNR metric, the Watershed algorithm gives the lowest results for the PSNR metric, with an average value for PSNR of 6.67dB, in contrast to Region Growing, which stands out significantly in this case with 9.73dB, while the F1 Score metric singles out K-means as the best in performance. With the best response (26.82% faster response than Watershed and 109.01% faster than Region Growing algorithm) but week precision.

articleTitle: Exploratory Data Analysis of NFL Player Performance and Impact of Age on Speed and Acceleration
abstract: This study examines the role of speed and agility in shaping player performance and game strategies in American football. By investigating the relationship between speed, acceleration, and age, the study uncovers trends that shed light on what makes players effective on the field. A comprehensive data analysis process, including preprocessing, feature extraction, and normalization, ensures a robust examination of these relationships. The findings highlight the complex dynamics between physical attributes and age, revealing insights into player development and performance dynamics. While offering valuable insights, the study also emphasizes the need for further investigation to account for outliers and refine the understanding of these critical performance factors. This study lays a solid foundation for improving how we evaluate and predict player potential, making a valuable contribution to performance analysis in football.

articleTitle: IoT-based farm management systems for modern agronomy
abstract: This article explores the design and implementation of IoT-based farm management systems to address pressing issues in agronomy, such as inefficient resource use, low crop yields, and high dependence on climatic factors. The problem lies in the need to optimize monitoring and management processes for agricultural land, particularly in the context of water scarcity and other resources. The goal of the article is to demonstrate how IoT systems can collect and analyses real-time data for automatic irrigation management and soil condition monitoring, thereby improving farmers' decision-making processes. The results of the study show that the application of IoT technologies enhances farm management efficiency, reduces water and energy consumption, and contributes to increased crop yields through more precise control of soil and plant conditions.

articleTitle: Cyber security risk in pervasive environments of unobtrusive cECG-monitoring system during driving
abstract: The development of pervasive healthcare systems in the automotive industry is enabled by unobtrusive acquisition systems for recording vital parameters of drivers and developed ML algorithms for driver health services. The paper proposes a pervasive system based on the acquisition of the cECG signal recorded through clothing during driving, the transmission of the cECG to the local device for processing cECG and extraction of cECG parameters, and the extracted parameters transmission via vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication channel to the cloud. The potential of cyber security risk in implementing the proposed system is identified.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of an Electromagnetic Vibratory Actuator Using CAD Software
abstract: The paper presents a model of an electromagnetic actuator that is used as an excitation element of vibratory conveyors and feeders. Considering the nonlinearity of the electromagnetic actuator, it is important to investigate its model and perform certain simulations. The model was checked with the EMWorks simulation package. Key simulation results are presented at the end of the paper.

articleTitle: Mitigating Misaligned Hall-Sensors in Brushless DC Motors Using Calibration Routine
abstract: Hall-Sensor-controlled brushless DC (BLDC) motors are commonly used in many applications due to their low cost and simple control. In a typical BLDC motor, a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) is controlled by a voltage source inverter (VSI) using the Hall sensor signals. Ideally, the three Hall sensors are spaced 120 degrees apart. However, due to manufacturing tolerances, the sensors’ actual position may differ, resulting in uneven conduction intervals and degradation of motor performance. To mitigate the misaligned Hall sensors, previous research proposed averaging the Hall sensor signals to achieve a steady state performance close to ideal. However, such averaging filters have a memory and may degrade the dynamic performance in fast transients. To ensure fast dynamic performance, this paper proposes a calibration routine and a correction lookup table that records and stores the identified errors, which are then corrected in run-time without compromising the dynamic performance. The proposed method is demonstrated on a typical industrial BLDC motor and has been shown to be very effective compared to previous methods.

articleTitle: Transformer Machine Learning Models for Time Series Electricity Power Forecasting
abstract: Time series forecasting is a cornerstone of predictive analytics in diverse domains, such as electricity power production (power plants) and transmission (power grids). Predicting electricity power is essential to renewable energy management. It helps optimize energy grids, reduce operational costs, and enhance power sustainability. The paper compares a few transformer and recurrent neural network models applied to time series data to estimate the wind farm's active power generation. The following machine learning models are described in detail: Patch Time Series Transformers (PatchTST), Time Series Transformers (TST), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). The prediction results of a known big data set (time series) are presented and analyzed in detail.

articleTitle: System modeling and analysis of advertising campaigns to increase their effectiveness
abstract: The paper considers the process of modeling advertising strategies using a systematic approach. The aim of the study is to evaluate and optimize advertising campaigns for various age groups of consumers, including teenagers, adults and pensioners. The model takes into account a variety of advertising channels, such as mobile advertising, television, mailing lists and billboards, analyzing their effectiveness for each group. As part of the study, experiments were conducted that showed that the initial period of an advertising campaign is critical for increasing the number of customers, after which the growth rate stabilizes. Optimization of advertising strategies has made it possible to increase the conversion efficiency of potential buyers into real ones. The results emphasize the importance of personalization of advertising campaigns depending on the age characteristics of the audience and the choice of advertising channels.

articleTitle: System for Testing Magneto-Electrical Properties of BCZT-CF/PVDF Flexible Composite Films
abstract: The paper presents a system for testing the magneto-electrical properties of flexible composite films based on barium calcium zirconium titanate (BCZT) and cobalt ferrite (CF) particles into a polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) Le. (BCZT-CF/PVDF). The system is based on a suitable electromagnet with a built-in air gap in which the films to be tested are placed and on an adequate current controlled power converter that performs pulse current excitation of the electromagnet The measured quantities are the current of electromagnet, magnetic induction in air gap and output voltage on the BZT-CF/PVDF device. At the end of the paper, the key experimental results obtained by measurements on the laboratory realized system are given.

articleTitle: Virtual Reality Solutions for Troubleshooting Autonomous Industrial Mobile Robots
abstract: This study aims to develop a virtual reality (VR) application to improve the fault detection and troubleshooting processes of autonomous industrial mobile robots. The complex systems and operating environments of autonomous robots make fault detection challenging for users, requiring effective and user-friendly solutions to overcome these difficulties. In this context, the Robot Operating System (ROS) was utilized to detect errors in robots and record these errors in a database. Thanks to the modular structure and robust communication infrastructure offered by ROS, faults in the robots were monitored and analyzed through ROS topics.This study demonstrates the effective use of VR technology in the maintenance and repair processes of autonomous industrial mobile robots. By integrating ROS-based data collection and fault detection into a VR environment for user training, robot operators are enabled to troubleshoot faults more quickly and effectively. In this way, it is aimed to achieve time and cost savings in industrial processes.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a 3D Social Mobile Robot with Artificial Intelligence for Teaching with Assistive Technology
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence is increasingly used in almost every sector of society for the analysis of large databases, pandemic forecasting, image recognition, machine translation, etc. Robots with artificial intelligence, for example, can assist people by performing tasks in extreme or dangerous environments (pandemic, in outer space, in explosive zones, etc.). Robots can also be used in the educational process of children with special educational needs, particularly for teaching children with autism spectrum disorder who may experience difficulties communicating with people. The paper presents the design and development process of a social robot with artificial intelligence for speech and faces emotions recognition. The aim of this paper is to present design process of low-budget 3D prototype of mobile social robot capable of speech recognition, as well as faces emotions recognition. The 3D robot components are designed and printed using 3D software and printing technologies. A seven-step algorithm has been presented for designing and implementation of the robot, ensuring it meets the functional requirements for assistive technology in education. The robot prototype has been implemented and tested with promising results.

articleTitle: Integrating Enterprise Identity Management with Blade Blockchain: A Practical Approach to Web3 Transition
abstract: This paper proposes a solution for integrating private blockchain technology into enterprise ecosystems, addressing challenges like operational complexity and security. Private blockchains enable enterprises to utilize decentralized technology while maintaining control over data and participants. The approach leverages existing identity access management systems and secure key management to assign and manage blockchain identifiers for enterprise users. This integration allows authenticated access to blockchain applications within existing workflows, simplifying adoption, reducing manual onboarding, and ensuring compliance with enterprise security policies. By bridging these gaps, the solution makes private blockchain technology more accessible for enterprise-scale deployment.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Analysis of Network Devices’ Configurations Based on the NETCONF Protocol
abstract: Network monitoring is crucial for minimizing errors and ensuring the efficient operation of network devices and infrastructure itself. Through network monitoring, one can provide users with the historical status of devices, allowing one to detect certain configuration changes and identify why they occur. With the increasing number of network devices in use today, it is challenging to ensure that active configurations are equal to their desired state. Although the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) is considerably more secure than the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) due to its use of TCP and encryption for communication, this does not prevent developers from making configuration errors, such as incorrect port numbers, total number of ports, wrong IP addresses, and similar issues. This paper presents an enhanced solution for controlling devices that use the NETCONF protocol for configuration management. By employing specific techniques to compare configurations in XML format and continuously monitoring devices on the network, the system can identify configuration errors and differences in comparison to the expected configuration. Additionally, by displaying historical results for a given device or statistical data of all devices over time, one can more easily identify the root cause of an error and thereby find its solution.

articleTitle: Effect of Orientation and Location on Surface Roughness of SLS PA12 parts
abstract: Selective Laser Sintering (SLS) is a widely used additive manufacturing process capable of producing complex geometries with high precision. However, the surface quality of SLS-printed parts, which directly affects their functional performance, remains a critical area of investigation. This study examines the influence of orientation and placement within the build chamber on the surface roughness parameters of PA12 polymer parts. Fifty parts were manufactured in five different orientations and categorized into three placement groups based on their spatial coordinates in the XY plane. The surface roughness parameters (Rt, Rz, RSm) were measured and analysed. The results show that orientation significantly affects SR parameters, with vertically oriented surfaces exhibiting higher roughness compared to horizontally oriented ones. The placement within the chamber displayed less pronounced but notable effects.

articleTitle: Pretrained Deep Learning Networks for Diabetic Foot Ulcer (DFU) Classification
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) present significant challenges in diagnosis, necessitating accurate classification of conditions, such as ischemia and infection. Current diagnostic approaches for DFU depend on comprehensive clinical assessments and imaging techniques, which are expensive and require significant resources. Traditional machine learning models often encounter challenges related to computational efficiency and precision, primarily stemming from the necessity of hand-crafted feature extraction. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs), specifically GoogleNet and AlexNet, in diagnosing DFUs for three classification problems: abnormality detection (normal vs. DFU), infection, and ischemia classifications. Unlike earlier research that focused on generalizing a model for a specific task, we are working on training our models for all three datasets. A sweeping parameters technique was employed to identify the optimal training hyperparameters setting, i.e., learning rate, minibatch size, and epoch number, to enhance the model efficiency. This study further examined the model performance change with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) as the binary classifier. The results showed that the pretrained models exhibited good prediction performance with acceptable accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score across all classification tasks ranging from 0.74-0.98. The ensemble of GoogleNet and SVM shows little to no improvement in the classification performance, while AlexNet+SVM revealed increased precision measure from 78.57 % to 82.42 % under the infection experiment. This paper concluded that further improvement of the proposed approach for DFU classification may offer a reliable solution for clinical application.

articleTitle: VLM-Enabled Network Experimentation: Case Study of Chanel Capacity in System Limited by η-μ Fading
abstract: In this paper, a micro-MRC receiver with L branches operating in a correlated gamma-shadowed η-μ fading channel is considered. For such a system, the channel capacity (CC) is determined based on the maximum signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the L branches at the input of the MRC receiver. The results are presented graphically to illustrate the impact of different system parameters on performance and the improvements that result from the advantages of combined diversity. Additionally, we introduce the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to make network experimentation more practical, using the previously presented expression as a case study. Moreover, a Vision Language Model (VLM) aided method aiming to make model-driven network design and experimentation more convenient is introduced and evaluated for the previously considered case study

articleTitle: Automation of Monitoring and Optimization of Docker Containers Using Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The increasing adoption of Docker containers in modern software development requires effective monitoring and optimization to ensure high performance and efficient resource utilization. This paper provides an overview of the various tools and technologies that leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to automate the monitoring and optimization of Docker containers. The authors explore the capabilities of AI-driven tools such as machine learning-based anomaly detection, predictive analytics, and automated resource management. By examining these tools, the authors highlight their benefits in enhancing container performance, scalability, and availability. Through comparative analysis, the strengths and limitations of each tool and their impact on container management are discussed. The findings underscore the potential of AI to revolutionize container monitoring and optimization, leading to more efficient and robust IT infrastructure.

articleTitle: Scheme development and experimental investigation of the cutting tool measurement method
abstract: The issues discussed in the article are related to the practical implementation of the cutting tool measurement method and experimental research in laboratory and close to production conditions. A measurement scheme has been developed to ensure the accuracy according to the method-specific conditions. With the experimental studies, concrete results have been obtained for the accuracy and the influence of the factors in their preparation. In order to evaluate in real conditions the accuracy that can be achieved with the measurement of the tool, an experiment was conducted, consisting in the processing of one installation of a part of rod material. The results obtained after measuring the sample surface with a micrometer and by touching it with the cutting tool are compared.

articleTitle: Leveraging a Specialized Screening System for Personalized Learning: A Statistical Evaluation of Student Performance Optimization
abstract: Personalized learning is recognized for its role in enhancing student performance by addressing individual learning needs. This study presents a statistical evaluation of a pedagogical experiment conducted via a specialized screening system designed to improve learning outcomes and provide the basis for data-driven customization of educational content. The system enables continuous tracking of student progress and provides real-time feedback for educators to fine-tune instructional strategies. Using a sample of elementary school students, we conducted an empirical study comparing traditional methods with personalized learning approaches facilitated by the screening system. Statistical analyses revealed performance improvements among students in the experimental group, particularly when personalized learning plans were used in the process. These findings underscore the screening system's potential as a valuable tool in personalizing education, paving the way for its broader integration within educational environments.

articleTitle: Development of a Responsive Web Application for Human Resource Management Using a NoSQL Database
abstract: The topic of this paper is the development of a responsive web application for human resource management using a NoSQL database. The technical goal of the paper is to demonstrate the possibility of developing a modern three-tier web application with the option of using MongoDB, a NoSQL database management system. From an economic perspective, the goal is to support business processes and assist in most activities related to modern human resource management in companies or organizations, thus creating conditions for faster and higher-quality decision-making by management concerning human resource management.

articleTitle: Universal Modified n-diode Solar Cell Models
abstract: Recently, different modified schemes of standard solar cell equivalent circuit have been proposed. In this paper, two variants of universal modified solar cell circuits are proposed. These models are specific because they provide analytic relation between solar cell current and voltage, which is expressed with Lambert W function. Some of the most recent numerical results from the available literature are also presented in the paper. The goal of this paper is to demonstrate that it is possible to obtain universal equivalent circuit of solar cells, regardless of the number of diodes used for the cells' model.

articleTitle: Design Considerations of an Outer Rotor PMSM for Ventricular Assist Devices
abstract: This study focuses on the design consideration of an embedded outer rotor Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM) tailored for a Ventricular Assist Device (VAD). The primary aim was to address the unique requirements of VAD systems, including compactness, efficiency, and integration without disrupting fluid flow dynamics. Key design constraints of the VAD structure were identified, and parametric swept processes were conducted with an emphasis on permanent magnet dimensions.
