articleTitle: From Visual Model to Source Code: Automated Fluent API Development Using Template-Based Code Generation in DSL Tools
abstract: The fluent API, also known as Internal DSL, is one of the concepts introduced primarily for the purpose of increasing readability and maintainability in the process of software development. It is most commonly used when there is a need to perform operations according to precisely defined rules that determine their possible orders. However, implementing a Fluent API by manual coding can divert focus from defining these rules toward technical implementation, increasing the risk of errors, unexpected behavior, and higher development costs. To address these challenges, a model-driven engineering (MDE) approach can be applied, enabling the visual design of the Fluent API model and its transformation into a code skeleton.This paper aims to present how the previously created graphical development tool, implemented as a Microsoft Visual Studio extension for modeling Fluent API, can be enhanced with model-to-text transformation in order to provide code generation of a fluent API structure. That objective is achieved by using the template-based code generation technique, implemented by enabling the execution of the appropriate T4 text templates. The proposed approach is validated by demonstrating a real-life fluent API example's code generation from its model, resulting in C# source files that contain classes, interfaces, and their corresponding methods.

articleTitle: Integration of Photovoltaic Systems into Smart Grids: Assessment of Impact on Grid Stability and Reliability
abstract: In order to research the advantages of usage of photovoltaic plants in smart grids, an analysis focused on the impact of photovoltaic systems on the stability and reliability of electrical grids is conducted in this paper. The paper addresses the technical aspects of integrating photovoltaic systems, including their variable production and how it affects the changes in electricity supply and demand in a real distributed power grid. Innovative technologies, such as energy storage devices and advanced communication systems, are also considered, which enable better control and management of the grid. The integration of a photovoltaic plant into a 20 kV network with consumers in the household and industrial categories, as well as an electric vehicle charging station, is analyzed with varying loads. The results obtained highlight the contribution of PV plants to the grid stability, reliability, voltage conditions, and total active and reactive power losses.

articleTitle: From Ratings to Balance: A Review of Glicko’s Role in Competitive Gaming Analytics
abstract: The Glicko and Glicko-2 have become foundational tools for evaluating skill levels and matchmaking efficiency in competitive gaming. Originally designed for chess, these systems have been adapted to esports to assess player performance, determine rankings, and balance matchmaking algorithms. This review explores the adoption and adaptation of the Glicko systems across various gaming genres, including real-time strategy, first-person shooters, and fighting games. It examines their implementation in professional and casual settings, highlighting benefits such as precision in skill differentiation and challenges like handling team-based dynamics, performance volatility, and data sparsity. Moreover, the paper identifies open questions in the field, including the applicability of Glicko systems in balancing game design, their integration with machine learning for predictive analytics, and the potential to address fairness in dynamic matchmaking scenarios. By synthesizing current research and practical applications, this review aims to provide a comprehensive overview and identify future research directions for leveraging the Glicko system to advance gaming analytics.

articleTitle: Out-of-Distribution Image Detection with Residual Spiking Neural Network Architectures
abstract: In recent years, the rapid advancements in machine learning models have led to significant improvements across various domains such as medical applications, autonomous systems, and image classification. However, real-world conditions often deviate from the controlled environments in which models are trained, leading to performance degradation. Out-of-distribution (OoD) detection has emerged as a critical task to address this issue, enabling models to identify when input data diverges from the training distribution. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), known for their energy efficiency and lower computational complexity compared to traditional models, have gained attention for their potential in OoD detection tasks. This paper explores the effectiveness of SNNs in OoD detection by introducing three distinct architectures: spike-Conv, spike-ResNet9, and spike-ResNet10, trained on widely used datasets. We present a comparative analysis of these architectures in terms of their accuracy and robustness in various OoD detection environments. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed spiking network architectures can effectively handle OoD detection with satisfcatory accuracy.

articleTitle: Statistical Modeling of Delivery Delays Due to Weather and Traffic Factors
abstract: This study investigates the influence of weather conditions and traffic flow dynamics on parcel delivery times. The main goal is to identify the factors contributing to delivery delays, which will help pinpoint key aspects that can improve logistics processes and enhance delivery accuracy. The Kruskal-Wallis test and Dunn’s post hoc analysis examined variations across data groups categorized by weather conditions (e.g., rain, snow, fog, storms) and traffic flow states (e.g., dense, congested, free-flowing, unobstructed). Additionally, a comparative approach was employed to assess the effects of different weather and traffic conditions. The results show that adverse weather conditions, such as rain and snow, combined with high traffic congestion, significantly increase delivery times compared to clear weather and normal or free-flowing traffic conditions. These findings offer valuable insights for future research and the optimization of logistics operations.

articleTitle: Sustainably enhancing olive oil production: intelligent system architecture
abstract: Olive oil production is a noteworthy economic activity in multiple places worldwide. Due to environmental degradation and lack of resources with population growth, there is a global tendency for more sustainable and efficient practices, driving the implementation of more responsible agricultural and industrial systems. This paper aims to develop an intelligent system architecture focused on optimizing the production of olive oil, improving product quality, reducing operational waste, and maximizing the efficient use of natural resources. Through the use of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies, the proposed solution aims to monitor and control the parameters of olive oil production automatically. In addition, the study addresses sensors already used in the market and existing systems to compare and seek improvements. The proposed architecture contains three layers: device, edge, and cloud computing layer, which are integrated and enable the implementation of a scalable and complete solution that allows real-time visualization and control of the production process.

articleTitle: Development of a Mechanical Thumb Prosthesis for Functional Restoration in Partial Amputations
abstract: Loss of thumb function due to partial amputations significantly affects the usability of the hand and the quality of life of users. Effective prosthetic solutions are required to restore functionality. In this study, we present the development and evaluation of a mechanical thumb prosthesis designed for people with partial amputations, based on anthropometric proportions of an average adult between 33 and 35 years old, with movements such as flexion and extension. A simulation was performed using a load of 5 N to evaluate the safety factor in the prosthesis structure. The results show a safety range between 2.991 and 15.00, which validates the resistance and robustness of the structure to the loads applied under normal conditions of use. This advancement provides users with a tool to enhance their autonomy and well-being, thereby improving their quality of life.

articleTitle: Backup of Cloud Data to On-Premises Locations
abstract: The paper focuses on maintaining backup copies of data transferred from a cloud platform to an on-premises location. When transferring data to an on-premises location to increase the security of system continuity, an additional backup copy of the data was made. Data security follows the legal and regulatory frameworks and prescribed standards, these standards are presented in the paper for both the European Union and the USA. The importance of the 3-2-1 backup rule is presented, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of this rule. The functionality of cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS and Google Cloud for data protection and methods for transferring backup copies using backup agents are presented, the paper describes an example in which Veeam Backup Agent is used. The advantages and disadvantages of backup storage tools such as Veeam, Acronis, Commvault, etc. are presented. The paper offers practical suggestions for implementing secure and efficient strategies in an IT environment.

articleTitle: Precision Agriculture Revolutionized: UAV-Based Detection of Leaffolders and Stem Borers in Ricefields using EfficientNetB1
abstract: The need for efficient pest management in rice cultivation is crucial due to the significant damage caused by pests like leaffolders and stem borers. Conventional manual inspection and sensory detection methods are labor-intensive and often inaccurate, leading to delayed and ineffective pest control measures. This study developed a system that uses unmanned areal vehicle (UAV) and machine learning algorithms to track the leaffolder and stem borer in rice fields. This system allows farmers to track the leaffolder and stem borer effectively and reliably without physically inspecting their entire field to determine the percentage affected by leaffolder and stem borer in the ricefield. Results indicate varying degrees of performance across different machine learning algorithms, with Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), consistently demonstrating superior accuracy, notably achieving 90.89% accuracy with EfficientNetB1. SVMs also exhibit commendable performance, excelling in complex decision frontier description. Decision trees, random forests, and transfer learning present nuanced performance characteristics, each offering unique strengths and limitations. The developed system tracked the disease between 73.22% and 90.89% using five groups with five tests per group. This study demonstrates the system’s effectiveness and opens avenues for further research and application in other areas of precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Students’ Attitude towards the Use of AI in Higher Education
abstract: Researching students’ awareness and attitudes towards AI tools is key to their successful integration into the educational process. This study aims to explore various aspects of AI usage in higher education. To achieve this goal, five research questions (RQ1-RQ5) were formulated and addressed through an online survey conducted from January 5 to 16, 2025, with 138 students. A total of 46 statements were evaluated using 5-point Likert scale. To quantitative assess participants’ responses, indices were calculated, including awareness, practical experience, benefits, risk, and innovation. The findings show that students are highly aware of the possibilities of using AI tools in education. The majority also believe they have relatively good practical experience with AI. Students’ perceptions of the benefits of AI applications and the level of concern about AI-related risks are moderately high. Students support the provided suggestions for more effective use of AI at a high extent.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Patient Triage Systems: Towards a Generic and Adaptable Model for Process Standardization
abstract: The continuous growth of the world’s population and extending life expectancy, as well as frequent natural disasters and emergencies, increase the demand for health services every day. One of the crucial elements for addressing this problem is triage – a critical process that enables healthcare providers to efficiently identify patients’ needs in terms of medical treatments and resources. However, the complexity of implementing an appropriate triage process has led to the development of various systems, each offering a unique approach to address this challenge.This paper presents a comparative analysis of different patient triage systems, focusing on their key characteristics, identifying their common and unique elements, and providing an understanding of their advantages and limitations. Relying on the findings of the conducted analysis, the paper proposes a generic model of the triage process, designed around universal components that provide a foundation for standardizing the process while maintaining the flexibility to adapt to specific requirements. The proposed generic model further can be employed as a basis for exploring opportunities to enhance the patient triage process through the application of model-driven engineering concepts and techniques.

articleTitle: Analyzing the elbow method in predicting the optimal number of clusters in Electronic Communications dataset
abstract: The aim of this article is to answer the question if elbow method giving us the best possible solution regarding the optimal number of clusters. Elbow method is one of the methodologies, which is often used in predicting the number of clusters. On the other side, it is always a question, how precise is a mathematical methodology in optimizing the number of clusters in comparison to qualitative methodologies. It is necessary to answer the question is elbow method giving us the best possible solution. It is crucial to answer what does it really mean in practical case, when analyzing the number of clusters in specific area in our case electronic communications development of different EU countries. The research is the combination of quantitative methodology and qualitative methodology. Elbow method itself is a quantitative methodology, which needs to be proved by qualitative method by analyzing and synthesis of the facts. In our case, we analyzed the sample of 32 different countries described by electronic communications development parameters and population density. The quantitative analyze was done in jupyter notebook environment by using the appropriate python code. It was proved by qualitative analyze using Rapidminer application (Alstair AI studio from 2024). K-means clustering was done by clustering the dataset into different number of clusters. By analyzing the results of clustering, we tried to prove the elbow method in this specific case by dividing the countries based on the electronic communications development parameters and population density. The result proved that in case of dataset of 32 samples, quantitative elbow method gave us satisfied result and separation in 3 clusters was optimal. It divided the countries in the most optimal way based on their specific characteristics regarding the electronic communications development parameters and population density.Elbow method is crucial and simple way to find optimal number of clusters, but all the quantitative methods need to be proved by qualitative method, where deep understanding of the research area is necessary.

articleTitle: Transforming Matrix Problem Solving with Intelligent Tutoring Systems
abstract: This paper presents the integration of optical character recognition (OCR) and advanced natural language processing (NLP) models for automated handling of matrices derived from images and textual inputs, all combined within an implemented chatbot. The motivation for choosing this topic arises from the practical experiences of the authors gained while working with groups of students who encounter the concept of matrices as part of their academic responsibilities. Through the analysis of their results and classroom interactions, it was observed that many students struggle with this area. This paper presents an innovative approach to enhancing matrix problem-solving by leveraging intelligent tutoring systems supported by High-Performance Computing, aiming to improve learning efficiency and student outcomes. By combining the EasyOCR framework and the Qwen2-Math-7B-Instruct model, operations such as transposition, addition, and multiplication of matrices are enabled. The system supports the input of one or two matrices, allowing the selection of operations through textual or image-based queries. The OCR component extracts numerical data from images, while the NLP model interprets user requests and executes operations accurately. The interface allows the addition of a second matrix image only when necessary, enhancing the system's intuitiveness and efficiency. The results of the recognition accuracy of the OCR model of image input matrices of different dimensions show a high level of accuracy of 95%, while for 2x2 matrices they reach an accuracy of 99%. This work contributes to the development of AI-powered tools for mathematical operations and holds potential applications in education.

articleTitle: Case study of performance degradation on the Xen hypervisor-based virtualization related to the native host
abstract: This paper conducts a comparative analysis of file system performance between a native operating system and Xen hypervisor-based virtualization. The study uses CentOS Stream 9 as both the native and guest operating system and employs Filebench for benchmarking purposes. Performance tests were carried out on the native operating system and within the Xen virtual environment, accommodating one to four virtual machines. A mathematical model was established for both the native and virtual environments, predicting that the native operating system would significantly outperform the virtualized one. The findings of this paper corroborate the model's predictions, demonstrating a substantial decline in file system performance due to virtualization.

articleTitle: The GreenTouch Digital Tool Web Development Planning: Comparative Analysis of Mental Health-Focused Web Solutions
abstract: This paper presents the planning and development of the GreenTouch digital tool, a web-based solution designed to improve mental health. The objective of this study was to identify the most suitable technologies for developing a scalable and user-friendly web application by reviewing seven mental health-focused platforms, analyzing their functionalities, and gaining insights into the tools and features they use for mental well-being. The methodology includes a systematic review of functionalities and technologies used in these applications. The analysis led to the identification of key technologies, which were then used to design two potential technology stacks for our solution. The results provide insights into the analysis of app features and the selection of technologies that ensure that both functional and aesthetic requirements are met, offering a strong foundation for the development of the desired web application. This research demonstrates the importance of balancing technical considerations with user experience factors when developing web-based mental health solutions.

articleTitle: Li-ion batteries equivalent circuit model parameter estimation from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements using neural networks
abstract: Although electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a powerful tool for understanding the internal processes in batteries, it is still not widely utilized in practical implementations. One of the reasons why that is the case is due to complexity of the equivalent circuit model (ECM) and time required for its analysis with the conventional approach, and lack of publicly available datasets for the machine learning approach. In this paper we suggest a new approach of estimating ECM parameters from EIS measurements using neural networks. For training of neural networks we propose using a completely synthetic dataset, bypassing the issue of the lack of the publicly available EIS datasets for Li-Ion batteries and only validating the trained model on experimentally measured dataset.

articleTitle: Biological Attributes in Classifying Protein Complex Membership
abstract: Proteins are crucial for various biological processes, often functioning as part of protein complexes that enable complex cellular activities. While traditional network-based approaches predict entire protein complexes by identifying dense subgraphs in protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks, this study focuses on predicting individual protein membership in complexes using their biological attributes. A binary classification model was developed, leveraging features derived from protein sequence properties, bag-of-words features, Kidera property factors, and amino acid physicochemical and biochemical attributes. Comprehensive feature selection methods were employed to enhance model performance. The proposed approach utilizes a Support Vector Classifier (SVC) and Random Forest (RF) model for classification, leveraging protein-specific characteristics as features. Experimental results demonstrate the SVC model’s potential for accurately classifying protein membership, providing valuable insights into protein functions and their roles within complexes.

articleTitle: Comparison of Neural Network and System Identification approaches for battery modeling and State of Charge estimation
abstract: A comparison of battery modeling results and state-of-charge estimation using neural networks and system identification approaches was conducted. These methods were applied to both simulation results and real battery measurements. Simulation data was used to determine the structure of the neural network and a linear regression model. Real battery data, consisting of two sets from two different batteries, was used to train and validate the models. The outcome of this study is black-box models derived from these two different approaches.

articleTitle: Methodology for Evaluating the Impact of DevOps Principles
abstract: The evolution of software development has led to the emergence of DevOps principles. DevOps principles enhance the integration between development and operations to achieve an uninterruptible and consistent flow of software delivery. The benefits of DevOps include the achievement of shared ownership of different parts of the process, automation of software development and testing, alongside the automation of infrastructure creation. Integrating DevOps, however, brings some challenges, primarily regarding its practical implementation. These challenges include cultural resistance, selection of imperfect tools and techniques, and the need for constant learning and improvement. Additionally, there is often lack of clarification and unity within an organization on if the implementation is successful, with differing views from different stakeholders. This compounds the practical challenges and makes it harder to improve over time. This paper aims to establish a new methodology for assessing the implementation of DevOps. Previous methodologies covered a wide range of questions, and this paper aims to improve on and complement areas covering adherence and understanding of DevOps principles by engineers and managers in companies. A study was conducted on whether our new methodology was able to evaluate the impact of DevOps across different teams, alongside whether its results conveyed a unison and unbiased representation from within the organization.

articleTitle: DCGMDL: Deep Conditional Generative Model for Dictionary Learning in Supervised Classification
abstract: In this paper, we propose the DCGMDL model, which utilizes a feed-forward neural network to exploit the inherent nonlinearity of data for dictionary learning. Unlike traditional dictionary learning methods that focus on learning linear dictionaries directly from nonlinear data in the original space, the DCGMDL approach introduces a novel framework by learning a linear dictionary in a transformed latent space. This design enables the model to effectively capture and utilize the nonlinear characteristics of input samples, resulting in a more robust and flexible approach to dictionary learning. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conducted experiments on image classification tasks using two benchmark datasets: Scenes-15 and ImageNet10. The experimental results demonstrate that the DCGMDL model achieves superior performance by leveraging the nonlinear properties of the data, highlighting its potential to overcome the limitations of conventional dictionary learning techniques.

articleTitle: Integrating Meteorological Data with Artificial Intelligence for Air Quality Prediction on Construction Sites
abstract: Air pollution, largely caused by activities in the construction sites, poses serious health and environmental risks to workers and people living nearby. This study focuses on predicting the concentrations of six major pollutants, i.e. PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, SO2, and O3. We train a Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) on each pollutant to forecast its levels twelve hours in advance. A window generator is used to map data into sequences, enabling the model to capture temporal patterns effectively. Extensive data pre-processing ensures accuracy, including handling missing values and transforming categorical variables. Specifically, the analysis of the pollutants is composed by the following steps: i) preparing the data, ii) building and training the model, iii) evaluating the model performance in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). We prove that LSTM performs outstandingly over other models, i.e. Random Forest and Artificial Neural Network. The obtained RMSE values ensure credibility and reliability of LSTM in air quality predictions. This predictive framework offers a practical approach for construction sites to manage air pollution and mitigate health and environmental impacts proactively.

articleTitle: Spectrogram-Based Fault Detection in Covered Conductors Using ResNet50V2 with SHAP and Grad-CAM Analysis
abstract: Partial discharges (PDs) in XLPE-covered conductors are critical precursors to insulation failure in medium-voltage networks. Despite advancements in radiometric PD detection using deep learning, the classification of multiple fault types remains underexplored, and model interpretability challenges hinder practical deployment. This study presents a spectrogram-based deep learning framework for classifying 12 PD fault types and background conditions using data from a BONI-WHIP antenna. By converting time-domain signals into spectrograms and employing a ResNet50V2 classifier, the framework achieves high multi-class classification accuracy. To enhance interpretability, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) identify the spectral features influencing predictions, aligning with known PD phenomena such as high-frequency emissions during discharges. The results demonstrate the potential for explainable AI in condition monitoring, with further validation under field conditions recommended to confirm its applicability.

articleTitle: Assessing Reproducibility and Accessibility in Hate Speech and Fake News Detection Datasets: A Literature Review (2023-2024)
abstract: This paper presents a systematic review of datasets for hate speech and fake news detection, published between 2023 and 2024. Using Kitchenham's methodology, we analyzed reproducible studies that provide comprehensive documentation and accessibility. These challenges compromise research validity, making it difficult to build effective and universally applicable detection models. Despite advancements in machine learning, the development of effective detection models has been hindered by inconsistencies in data quality and annotation standards. This study highlights the need for high-quality, diverse datasets that adhere to reproducibility standards and emphasizes the importance of incorporating multimodal data to improve model performance.

articleTitle: FRUITrank: A Web Application for the Selection of Plum Varieties Using the MARCOS MCDM Method
abstract: Efficient decision-making in fruit production involves evaluating multiple criteria, such as yield, fruit quality, and resistance, to rank available alternatives. Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) methods provide a structured and objective framework for such tasks. This paper presents a web-based application named FRUITrank, designed to implement the MARCOS MCDM method for ranking and selection of plum varieties. The application uses a predefined set of criteria, whose weights were determined externally by using other MCDM methods. By leveraging a simple and intuitive interface, the application aims to overcome barriers to the practical adoption of MCDM methods among researchers and fruit producers, such as mathematical complexity and lack of accessible tools. The application was tested using a set of 11 criteria relevant to plum production, demonstrating its capability to deliver reliable and transparent rankings. This paper builds upon prior research in MCDM applications for agriculture, offering a practical solution for producers and researchers to enhance decision-making processes. Future improvements to the developed tool may include automated criteria weight calculation and broader applicability across various agricultural contexts.

articleTitle: ChatGPT and Creation of Tests in ESP
abstract: The paper investigates the application of ChatGPT in the creation of tests for English for Specific Purposes (ESP). After the introduction, it discusses the fundamental role of testing in ESP, presents various test classifications, and examines the possible functions and benefits of test creation software. The sections that follow deal with the use of ChatGPT for the creation of language assessments and tests, at first through literature review and then through a more specific discussion on the use of ChatGPT for the generation of ESP assessments and tests, dealing both with practical use, issues, benefits, advantages, flaws and drawbacks and with ethical and aesthetical aspects of such creations. The final section gives some conclusions and recommendations.

articleTitle: Performance and Efficiency of Blockchain in Telecommunications: A Comparative Study with Traditional Systems
abstract: This work looks into the utilization of blockchain technology within the telecommunications sector, emphasizing enhancements in security, privacy, and efficiency of data management. The “TelecomSecurity” smart contract, demonstrates blockchain’s features of decentralization and immutability, enabling robust user data protection, transparent identity management, and process automation. The paper focuses on protection mechanisms and resource optimization, showcasing detailed metrics of performance and gas consumption compared to traditional environments like Python and Flask. Additionally, it includes an analysis of the study “Blockchain technology empowers telecom network operation” by Dinh C. Nguyen, Pubudu N. Pathirana, and Ming Ding, published in IEEE Communications Magazine 2020, to discuss the blockchain’s potential to enhance operations within telecom networks, especially when integrating 5G technologies. The research establishes parallels between theoretical insights and practical findings, underscoring the blockchain’s relevance and use cases in real-world telecom scenarios. It also discusses potential applications in 5G networks and IoT devices, positioning blockchain as a transformative technology for the digital age, enhancing security, lowering costs, and improving operational efficiency. More specifically, this study explores how blockchain-based decentralized user management and smart contract automation can enhance telecom service agreements, reducing reliance on centralized authorities while improving transparency and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Process Mining Meets BPM: A Conceptual Solution for Automating Production Planning in Manufacturing
abstract: Successful automation, digitization, and management of production planning processes often require a comprehensive approach. To modernize how business processes are executed, this research explores the potential of integrating business process management (BPM) with the process mining (PM) approach. The analysis of the production planning process in a mid-sized manufacturing company in Serbia was executed in order to visualize current flows, as well as to identify bottlenecks, deviations, and unnecessary steps. Process data, i.e. the event log was imported in a process mining tool – Disco, and obtained results were used to propose process improvements, including better allocation of resources, reduction of waiting time and automation of frequently repeated tasks. Therefore, this paper studies the potential of implementing process mining in achieving production planning automation.

articleTitle: Building and Utilizing a Specialized Chatbot in Physics Education – Experiment and Results
abstract: This article presents an experiment involving the development and using of a specialized chatbot, named PhysicsGPT, in physics education. The experiment was conducted with 7th-grade students during their study of the topic "Light and Sound". PhysicsGPT was created using the Zapier platform, which allows for the creation of chatbots without programming. The chatbot provides students with personalized guidance, examples, and facts, assisting them in understanding the material. The study involved 22 students who used PhysicsGPT to develop coursework on a topic related to the total internal reflection of light. A survey of students' opinions revealed that they highly valued the chatbot's usefulness and ease of use. A significant portion of the students found the information provided to be relevant and easy to understand. The analysis uncovered a moderate correlation between the chatbot's ease of use and its perceived usefulness, as well as between the understanding of the lesson and the overall impression of working with the chatbot.

articleTitle: Barriers and Benefits of Serious Games and AI in Education
abstract: Today, as technology and games have become integral to everyday life, challenges arise in maintaining and enhancing the focus on learning. Although digital games offer excellent opportunities for innovative ways of acquiring knowledge, distraction and how best to balance the entertainment side with the education objectives also create problems. In such an environment, the main goal is to utilize games as motivational tools that engage students while contributing to the development of critical thinking, problem-solving, and creativity. Research is based on a survey among students and teachers from three partner countries, targeting their perception of Serious Games and AI as an educational means in which barriers and obstacles may arise when including it in the teaching and learning process. These data will help formulate recommendations on how to optimize the use of Serious Games within educational systems across three diverse cultures and educational practices.

articleTitle: Contribution of the YOLO model to the UXO detection process
abstract: This paper explores the application of the YOLOv5 deep learning model for detecting unexploded ordnance (UXO) using UAV aerial imagery. UXO poses a global humanitarian and ecological threat, necessitating AI-driven solutions for real-time detection in complex environments. Integrating YOLOv5 with UAV systems, the study enhances detection accuracy, operational efficiency, and safety in high-risk areas. Using 12,600 annotated images, the model achieves a 97.77% mAP with optimized precision-recall balance. Advanced data augmentation and hyperparameter tuning further improve robustness. The proposed framework enables scalable, real-time UXO detection, significantly improving demining operations. Findings also support broader applications in disaster response, public safety, and military operations, demonstrating AI's critical role in global security and humanitarian efforts.

articleTitle: Innovating Real Estate Business Models with Blockchain
abstract: Blockchain technology has emerged as a potential enabler of novel business models in the real estate sector, which is poised for significant change. This article provides a comprehensive review of the research on innovative blockchain-based strategies for real estate. It clarifies the problems associated with traditional real estate business structures and explores blockchain as a disruptive technology. Through the literature review, several unique blockchain-enabled business models are identified, including real estate asset tokenization, decentralized marketplaces, peer-to-peer transactions, and fractional ownership. The potential benefits of these models—such as improved liquidity, accessibility, and efficiency—are demonstrated. Additionally, blockchain's capacity for automating processes via smart contracts, enhancing transparency in title management, and mitigating fraud risks is examined. The paper also discusses the challenges and limitations associated with implementing these blockchain-based models, highlighting technical complexity, legal and regulatory barriers, cybersecurity risks, and market adoption hurdles. It emphasizes the importance of developing scalable, interoperable blockchain frameworks that integrate seamlessly with existing real estate infrastructures. The main finding is that blockchain has the potential to transform the real estate industry by creating new, disruptive business models. However, further research, regulatory adjustments, and real-world implementations are needed to fully realize the advantages of blockchain-based innovations and foster a supportive real estate ecosystem.

articleTitle: Possibilities of ANN Application for Condition Monitoring of Power Transformers Using DGA
abstract: The transformer is one of the most important elements of the power system. Monitoring the behavior of the transformer is necessary in order to avoid catastrophic failures and costly interruptions in operation. Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) is a conventional technique that is widely used for diagnosing initial failures in transformers. All classical approaches have limitations because they cannot accurately diagnose all faults, that is, a large number of transformer states remain undefined. These methods are characterized by lower accuracy. In order to improve the accuracy of diagnostics in conventional dissolved gas analysis (DGA), an artificial neural network (ANN) has been applied to the conventional IEC and Rogers method of relationships. The chosen ANN approach of DGA gives very satisfactory results because it is now possible to classify all transformer states. The ANN was simulated and tested in the MATLAB R2022b environment with an accuracy of over 85%. By comparing ANN to the IEC and Rogers methods of relationships, which have an accuracy of 5060%, this approach successfully addresses the limitations associated with conventional methods of relationships. ANN has thus developed into an excellent tool in the field of diagnostics of power transformer failures.

articleTitle: Security Challenges and Mitigation Strategies for CAN-Based Protocols: A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: The Controller Area Network (CAN) protocol is the backbone of many critical communication systems in automotive, industrial, and embedded applications. Despite its widespread adoption, CAN-based protocols, such as J1939, CANopen, NMEA 2000, and others, face inherent security vulnerabilities due to their lack of robust authentication and encryption mechanisms. This research examines the security challenges associated with CAN and its derivative protocols, focusing on potential exploits such as message spoofing, eavesdropping, denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, and unauthorized data access. Unlike previous studies, this work comprehensively reviews defense strategies, techniques, and countermeasures across multiple CAN-based protocols, aiming to identify all possible security solutions in a unified analysis. In addition, it evaluates current industry solutions, including encryption overlays, intrusion detection systems (IDS), and protocol enhancements, while considering trade-offs between security and performance metrics, such as network traffic load, latency, and scalability. By analyzing existing approaches, this research identifies gaps in current implementations and explores innovative strategies to enhance security while maintaining network efficiency. The findings contribute to developing more resilient communication frameworks in CAN networks.

articleTitle: The Power of Words: Leveraging Deep Learning Techniques to Predict Hotel Ratings from User Reviews
abstract: User reviews have become a crucial resource for insights into customer experiences, especially in the hospitality industry. Building upon prior research, this paper presents a deep learning methodology for predicting hotel ratings through analyzing the text of user reviews. By applying advanced natural language processing techniques and neural networks, we build a framework that analyzes review titles, text, and sets of tags to predict hotel ratings. Moving beyond conventional sentiment analysis, this model identifies more complex linguistic patterns, improving rating prediction accuracy. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of deep learning techniques, including word embeddings and recurrent neural networks, in extracting key features from user content. This study highlights the potential of AI in the tourism sector, providing an innovative approach to reputation management and customer satisfaction.
